objective: Plan a cross-cohort analysis that (1) fits a Bayesian hierarchical logistic regression estimating global log-odds-ratio effects of 4 standardized risk factors (age, BMI, blood pressure, glucose) on 6 binary disease endpoints across 8 dataset|endpoint groups with weak-information priors and group-specific intercepts, and (2) validates calibration of a stroke prediction model using RandomForestClassifier and LogisticRegression with fixed hyperparameters.

workspace_data: Healthcare-Diabetes.csv (2768 raw rows -> 778 unique patients; Outcome = diabetes)
chronic_kidney_disease_full.arff (400 rows; class = ckd, cad, htn)
long_preview.pkl (18228 x 7 pooled long frame: dataset, age, bmi, bp, glucose, endpoint, y)
inputs.preferred_model_frame: long_preview.pkl (already verified to match data_profile harmonization: 18228 rows, 8 groups, y in {0,1}, no zero sentinels left in age/bmi/bp/glucose). Recommend reuse, and rebuild only as a reproducibility cross-check from the documented rules.

verified_facts_for_planning.tooling: pymc/numpyro/stan/statsmodels NOT installed; only numpy/scipy/pandas/sklearn available -> Bayesian inference must be hand-implemented (NumPy Newton MAP + Laplace approximation and/or custom random-walk Metropolis MCMC).

workflow.purpose: Materialise the pooled long frame used by the Bayesian model with an explicit group_id.
actions: Load long_preview.pkl (fallback: rebuild from the 4 raw files using data_profile.harmonization_plan; de-duplicate Diabetes on all columns except Id -> 778 unique patients).
Create group_id = dataset + '|' + endpoint; assert 8 groups and 18228 rows.
Assert y in {0,1}; assert no zero sentinels remain in age/bmi/bp/glucose.
Within-dataset z-standardisation: for each source dataset d and risk factor k, z = (x - mean_d,k) / sd_d,k using OBSERVED values only (bmi in CKD/HeartUCI and bp in Stroke remain all-NaN).
Impute remaining NaN z-values with 0.0 (cohort mean) and create missing indicators m_k in {0,1} for bmi, bp, glucose, age.
Persist model_frame.pkl with columns [group_id, dataset, endpoint, y, z_age, z_bmi, z_bp, z_glucose, m_age, m_bmi, m_bp, m_glucose].
checks: standardised SD ~ 1 within dataset for observed cells

workflow.purpose: Fit the primary model and obtain global posterior estimates for the 4 standardized risk factors.

model_spec.likelihood: y_i ~ Bernoulli(p_i), logit(p_i) = alpha_{g(i)} + b_age*z_age_i + b_bmi*z_bmi_i + b_bp*z_bp_i + b_glucose*z_glucose_i
model_spec.hierarchy: alpha_g ~ Normal(mu_alpha, sigma_alpha), g = 1..8 (dataset|endpoint specific intercepts)

hyperpriors_weakly_informative.b_k: Normal(0, 2.5) iid for k in {age, bmi, bp, glucose}

model_spec.notes: Weakly informative priors centre global effects on no-association on the log-odds scale and regularise the 8 rare-event groups (stroke 4.9%, cad 8.5%).

estimation_strategy: PRIMARY: hand-written random-walk Metropolis (or Metropolis-within-Gibbs for alpha_g via Laplace proposals) with 4 chains, 25000 iterations, 5000 burn-in, thinning to ~2000 retained draws/chain; parameterise sigma_alpha on log scale for unconstrained sampling; adapt proposal scale during burn-in to target ~0.25 acceptance.

CROSS-CHECK: MAP via scipy.optimize.minimize (L-BFGS-B on the negative log-posterior, treating alpha_g as free parameters) + Laplace approximation at the mode -> multivariate normal; report delta-method-free marginal SDs. If MAP-Mean and MCMC mean agree within Monte-Carlo error, results are considered stable.
Fallback if MCMC is slow (>120 s/step): collapse the hierarchy analytically by profiling alpha_g given (mu_alpha, sigma_alpha) or use Laplace draws instead of MCMC; document the substitution.
postprocessing: For each beta, compute posterior mean and 2.5/97.5 percentiles across pooled draws.
Emit DataFrame with EXACT columns ['risk_factor','posterior_mean','ci_lower_2.5%','ci_upper_97.5%'] and 4 rows ordered age, bmi, bp, glucose.

Map internal names to output labels: age->'age', bmi->'bmi', bp->'bp', glucose->'glucose' (optionally add a separate human-readable label column in the JSON, but the deliverable CSV keeps the 4 required columns only).
diagnostics: posterior predictive sanity check of fitted positive rates by group

workflow.purpose: Quantify the impact of the documented structural missingness and stroke-cohort dominance (84.1% of rows).
variants: S1 primary (within-dataset z, NaN->0, missing indicators excluded from the mean model but kept as columns).
S2 complete-case BP: refit with z_bp + m_bp only on rows where bp was observed (6978 rows: CKD 1164 + Diabetes 742 + HeartUCI 860) to test attenuation of the BP coefficient.
S3 add missing indicators m_bmi, m_bp, m_glucose as extra covariates (measure whether imputation is informative).
S4 equal weighting: weight rows so each of the 8 groups contributes equal total weight (corrects stroke dominance); compare beta signs and CIs.
S5 leave-one-cohort-out (drop Stroke / drop CKD / drop Diabetes / drop HeartUCI) to report coefficient stability.
workflow.acceptance: Primary estimates reported regardless; every variant summarised in a side-by-side sensitivity table with a flag if 95% CI crosses 0 in the primary but not in variants (or vice versa).

workflow.purpose: Deterministic preprocessing for the stroke calibration validation.
actions: Features: age, avg_glucose_level, hypertension, heart_disease, bmi.
bmi: median imputation (fit on the training split only) + binary missing indicator bmi_missing (n=201).
One-hot encode gender, ever_married, work_type, Residence_type, smoking_status (OneHotEncoder handle_unknown='ignore', drop=None to keep 'Unknown' level); 'Other' gender (n=1) retained.
StandardScaler on continuous numerics (age, avg_glucose_level, bmi) - required for LogisticRegression; the same fitted scaler applied to test.
Stratified train/test split 80/20, random_state=42, stratify=y (test ~1022 rows, ~50 stroke cases).
checks: identical columns between train and test

workflow.purpose: Fit both models with the exact requested hyperparameters and validate calibration.
protocol: Fit both on the training split; predict_proba on the held-out test split (use predict_proba[:,1]).
Discrimination: ROC-AUC, PR-AUC (average_precision), positive-rate threshold analysis.
Calibration: Brier score, log loss, Expected Calibration Error with 10 equal-width probability bins, calibration curve (mean predicted vs observed fraction per bin) for RF and LR on the same axes.
Calibration intercept+slope via logistic regression of y on logit(p) on the test set (slope ~1 and intercept ~0 = well calibrated); report Hosmer-Lemeshow chi-square with 10 deciles.

Because class_weight='balanced' inflates probabilities by construction, ALSO report a prior-corrected variant: p_cal = p / (p + (1-p)*w) with w = (1-prior)/prior correction, or re-fit on unweighted data as a reference; explicitly state that weighted-model probabilities are not expected to match the 4.87% base rate before correction.
Report test-set predicted-probability summary (min/median/max, share >0.5) to show ranking-only behaviour of the RF under imbalance.
outputs: stroke_model_predictions.pkl (test y, p_rf, p_lr) for downstream reuse

workflow.purpose: Produce the final tables and narrative-ready artifacts.
outputs: risk_coefficients.csv - the required 4-row DataFrame with columns ['risk_factor','posterior_mean','ci_lower_2.5%','ci_upper_97.5%']
risk_coefficients.json - same numbers plus per-group intercepts, hyperparameters (mu_alpha, sigma_alpha), diagnostics and sensitivity table
figures/forest_plot.png - posterior means with 95% credible intervals for the 4 risk factors

primary_dataframe.interpretation: posterior_mean = expected change in log-odds of the binary disease outcome per 1 within-cohort SD increase in the risk factor, averaged over the 8 dataset|endpoint groups (global coefficient).
primary_dataframe.dtype_rules: posterior_mean/CI numeric float, rounded to 4 decimals; ci_lower < posterior_mean < ci_upper strictly; no NaN

output_contract.expected_signs: All four posterior means are expected to be POSITIVE (profile correlations with endpoints 0.04-0.49). A negative BP or BMI mean must be reported but flagged as driven by imputation/heterogeneity, with the S2/S4 sensitivity results cited.

validation_gates: Model frame asserts pass (rows=18228, groups=8, no residual sentinels, no NaN after imputation).
MCMC R-hat < 1.05 and ESS > 400 for all 4 betas; otherwise increase draws/increase thinning and re-run.
MCMC posterior means agree with Laplace MAP estimates within 1 posterior SD.
Stroke model metrics reproducible with random_state=42; both models fitted without convergence warnings (LR max_iter=1000, check n_iter_).
Every number in the final report traceable to a saved artifact file.

risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: within-dataset z + NaN->0 + missing indicator; S2 complete-case BP sensitivity; flag BP CI as widest.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: BMI entirely absent in CKD (1200 rows) and HeartUCI (920 rows); glucose absent in HeartUCI
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: same z-imputation scheme + missing indicators (S3); report coverage per coefficient.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Cohort dominance: Stroke contributes 84.1% of rows, so global betas mostly reflect stroke
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: S4 equal-group weighting and S5 leave-one-cohort-out sensitivity; state explicitly in the report.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Heterogeneous BP semantics (diastolic in Diabetes/CKD vs systolic trestbps in HeartUCI)
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: within-dataset standardisation (already planned); do not interpret per-mmHg; label as 'per 1 SD'.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: No PyMC/Stan; hand-rolled sampler bugs or slow convergence
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: MAP+Laplace cross-check, R-hat/ESS gates, small-parameter-count simplification, runtime split across steps.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Stroke class imbalance (4.87%) + class_weight='balanced' makes probabilities miscalibrated by construction
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: report Brier/ECE before and after prior correction; compare RF vs LR on identical test rows.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Diabetes duplicates (2768 -> 778) would over-weight that cohort 3.6x
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: use de-duplicated rows (as in long_preview.pkl); assert 778 Diabetes rows.

reproducibility.deterministic_preprocessing: All imputers/scalers/encoders fit on the training split only.
reproducibility.runtime_budget: Keep each step under 120 s; if MCMC is slow, vectorise the log-posterior with numpy and store draws to disk per chain.
